summary.text: A tidal stream generator, often called a tidal turbine, is a machine that draws energy from moving water, especially tides, much as a wind turbine does from air.
Because water is about 800 times denser than air, a tidal turbine can make significant power at flow speeds far lower than comparable wind speeds.
Among the four main forms of tidal power generation, tidal stream generators are the cheapest and the least ecologically damaging.

facts.label: First conceived
facts.value: In the 1970s, during the oil crisis

facts.label: Main types
facts.value: Six, as recognized by the European Marine Energy Centre

items.prompt: A tidal turbine and a wind turbine of the same size produce the same power. Roughly how fast is the water moving compared with the wind?
items.explain: Power depends on the medium's density and the cube of its speed, so water at nearly one-tenth of wind speed gives the same power.

items.prompt: Why can a single tidal turbine produce significant power even when the water is flowing slowly?

options.label: Water is much heavier per volume than air
Seawater conducts electricity to the blades
Tidal currents never stop flowing at all
Its blades are always far longer than a windmill's

items.explain: Water is about 800 times as dense as air, so one generator can give significant power at low flow speeds.

items.prompt: A prototype tidal turbine in New York's East River ran into trouble with its 2006 and 2007 versions. What went wrong?

options.label: Ice jammed the rotor every winter

items.explain: The strong currents challenged the design: the blades of the 2006 and 2007 prototypes broke, and reinforced turbines replaced them in 2008.

items.prompt: A seabed turbine with fixed blades must face a new direction each time the tide reverses. When is the sensible moment to turn it?

options.label: At the strongest point of the flow
Only once a year, for maintenance
In the slack water between tides

items.explain: AR turbines are rotated with each tidal exchange during the slack period between tides, then held at the best heading for the next tide.

items.prompt: Investors ask why no single tidal turbine design has become the standard. What is the main gap?
items.explain: Prototypes have shown promise, but they have not operated commercially for long enough to establish performance and returns on investment.

items.prompt: Tidal stream turbines were first conceived in the 1970s. During which event of that decade did the idea appear?
items.explain: Tidal stream generators were first conceived in the 1970s, during the oil crisis.
